# Lab 8.4: Assertions & Data Quality Tests

## What We Are Going to Do
Add built-in assertions to a model and write a custom assertion, then see a failing assertion stop the run.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Add built-in assertions.** Edit `stg_orders.sqlx`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">config {
  type: "view",
  assertions: {
    uniqueKey: ["order_id"],
    nonNull: ["order_id", "user_id"],
    rowConditions: ["num_of_item &gt; 0", "status IN ('complete','shipped','processing','returned','cancelled')"]
  }
}</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Write a custom assertion.** `definitions/assertions/no_future_orders.sqlx`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">config { type: "assertion" }

SELECT * FROM ${ref("stg_orders")}
WHERE created_at &gt; CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   An assertion fails if its query returns any rows.

3. **[Console] Make one fail.** Change the row condition to `num_of_item > 3`. Start an execution with **Include dependents**. The assertion fails, and actions that depend on it are skipped.

4. **[CLI] Look at the assertion views.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq ls lab08_assertions
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lab08_assertions.`YOUR_PROJECT_lab08_stg_orders_assertions_rowConditions`'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Each assertion is a view. Querying it shows the rows that broke the rule. Replace the view name with the one shown by `bq ls`.

5. **[Console] Put the rule back** to `num_of_item > 0` and run again.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Built-in assertions | `uniqueKey`, `nonNull`, `rowConditions` |
| Custom assertion | Fails if it returns rows |
| Failure | Dependent actions skipped |
| Debugging | Query the assertion view |
